newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco sees costs falling sharply by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Codelco sees costs falling sharply by 2001.

text.p: Chile's state copper copper company Codelco expects its direct costs to fall around ten cents a pound over the next four years to $0.40 in 2001 from some $0.50 this year, said president Marcos Lima.
"The increase in output together with the reduction in the workforce...and improvement in management have resulted in a sharp increase in productivity," Lima told a mining seminar.
The start-up of the Radomiro Tomic copper mine early next year will have an immediate impact on the corporation's costs.
The 150,000 tonne a year pit will produce copper cathodes using low-cost heapleaching technology which is much cheaper than the traditional concentrator and smelter.
Lower costs and a rise in output should mean pre-tax profits will climb over 50 percent in the next four years to around $1.6 billion -- provided copper prices average $1/lb, said Lima.
"If our calculations are extended to the period 1997-2001 with the increase in production (during this period), pre-tax profits should rise by $486 million or 53 percent," he said.
Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, reported pre-tax earnings of $1.1 billion last year.
Lima said the corporation's copper output will increase to 1.6 million tonnes by 2001 from 1.22 million last year.
The rise in production is due to the start-up of the Radomiro Tomic pit, the expansion at the Andina division and the opening later this year of the Esmeralda mine at the El Teniente division.
